column11: the house Part D convention (backend/gross_to_net.py, PART_D_CONVENTION): CMS Part D spending is gross of manufacturer rebates, and the book deducts half on a Part D anchor. The module measures that convention against every CMS Maximum Fair Price in the demand table and lands at a median 96% of the negotiated annual price across the nine cycle-one drugs that carry both
column12: Calibrated against this drug's own negotiated price, which is unusual and worth stating. Otezla was selected for Medicare negotiation and CMS set a Maximum Fair Price of $1,650 per 30-day equivalent supply effective 2027-01-01 (negotiated_prices, IPAY 2027, as of 2025-11-25, ten NDCs all at the same figure). The 31,045 beneficiaries of 2024 filled 6.955 thirty-day equivalents each, so the same patients at the negotiated price would be $11,476, which is 34.1% of the $33,662 gross: a Medicare-only reading would put this row at 0.659 rather than 0.5. The convention is kept because the layer it prices is a US pool and not a Medicare one, and a Maximum Fair Price is a ceiling CMS negotiated for a drug seven or more years past launch, below what commercial payers pay. At 0.5 the net is $16,831 a beneficiary-year, 1.47 times the negotiated Medicare equivalent, which is the direction a commercial-inclusive blend should sit. Replace this with 0.659 if the book ever prices a Medicare-only layer on Otezla

column11: the approved disease, approved 2025-07-23. FDA approved NDA 205437 supplement 14 on that date (Drugs@FDA, efficacy supplement, AMGEN INC) and the current label reads 'OTEZLA is indicated for the treatment of adult patients and pediatric patients 6 years of age and older and weighing at least 20 kg with active psoriatic arthritis' (openFDA drug/label, effective_time 20260902). Juvenile psoriatic arthritis is the disease both registered studies enrol: NCT04804553 (PEAPOD) is 'Apremilast in Children From 5 to Less Than 18 Years of Age With Active Juvenile Psoriatic Arthritis', 60 participants, and NCT05767047 is its long-term extension, 48 participants. A ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 search for apremilast and juvenile returns these two and no other, so the enthesitis-related arthritis half of the book's pool for this unit has no apremilast study behind it
